comparator.sourceNotes: The 135 EC major includes eight first-year courses, three research methods courses, one thematic package, two advanced courses and a thesis. This example uses the welfare-state package and illustrates advanced study in philosophy and history. The remaining 45 EC is open for electives.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target names no thematic package. Utrecht presents four equally weighted interdisciplinary packages with no general default. The cohort regulations list Challenges to the Welfare State first. Their two advanced-choice lists likewise place Topics in Philosophy and Advanced Disciplinary Course in History first. The illustration follows this published order independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The welfare and public policy plan draws on all four PPE disciplines. The other plans develop the separate directions of market regulation and environmental governance. Utrecht’s integrated thematic package and required interdisciplinary thesis remain distinct.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Use 45 EC for choices such as electives, a minor, study abroad or an internship. At least 15 EC must be at intermediate level.
Both develop qualitative research design and methods. UCR approaches them through sociology.
Both use research design and statistics to assess evidence. UCR introduces methods across several fields.
Utrecht’s published curriculum gives a working title. UCR develops formal logic in a separate course.
Utrecht requires a thesis that draws on two PPE disciplines. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Both build ethical reasoning. Utrecht applies it directly to questions of public policy.
Both study political authority, rights and competing ideas about just institutions.
This example shows a philosophy option. The topic can vary.
Both compare political institutions and how democracies work. UCR also studies authoritarian regimes and democratic backsliding.
Both examine how policy is made. The UCR course develops policy analysis and memo writing through a case study.
Students bring together the PPE disciplines to investigate a question from the welfare-state package.
Both use microeconomic models to study markets and decisions. The UCR course also examines behavioral departures from standard models.
Both examine aggregate economic activity and policy. UCR gives particular attention to open economies.
Both examine social insurance and redistribution. Utrecht also considers how welfare institutions balance competing values.
Utrecht studies debates in global economic history. UCR uses modern history and the history of empires to examine industrialization and economic institutions.
Both study how political institutions and ideas developed. The UCR course covers broader themes in modern history.
Utrecht studies how welfare states developed and changed. UCR history and sociology provide wider context.
This example shows a history option. Utrecht has published a provisional course title.

notes.text: Utrecht teaches philosophy, politics, economics and history through an integrated major, a thematic package and a required thesis. At UCR, students combine courses from these fields and may pursue independent research separately.

audience.programmeDescription: This English-taught bachelor uses philosophy, politics, economics and history to study how institutions work and how societies make collective decisions.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example shows the welfare-state package. The UCR options emphasize welfare and public policy, market regulation, or environmental governance.
